slot.brief: Statements comparing classical (reducing) smog and photochemical (oxidising) smog – constituents, time of formation, health effects; choose the correct set.

stem:
Consider the statements about $smog.
I$. Classical smog forms in cool, humid conditions and contains smoke, particulates and $	ext{SO}_2$$.
II$. Photochemical smog forms in sunlight from $	ext{NO}_x$ and hydrocarbons and is $oxidising.
III$. Photochemical smog generally does not irritate the eyes or respiratory $tract.
Which$ set of statements is correct?

verdicts.working: I and II are true: classical smog forms in cool, humid conditions, while photochemical smog forms in sunlight from NOₓ and hydrocarbons and is oxidising. III is false because photochemical smog can irritate the eyes and respiratory tract.

working:
I: true; classical smog is associated with cool, humid conditions and reducing pollutants.\nII: true; sunlight-driven reactions of $\text{NO}_x$ and hydrocarbons produce oxidants.\nIII: false; photochemical smog can irritate the eyes and respiratory tract.

Independent check: I and II are true: classical smog forms in cool, humid conditions, while photochemical smog forms in sunlight from NOₓ and hydrocarbons and is oxidising. III is false because photochemical smog can irritate the eyes and respiratory tract.
solution: Classical smog forms in cool, humid conditions and contains smoke, particulates and $\text{SO}_2$, so I is true. Photochemical smog forms when sunlight acts on $\text{NO}_x$ and hydrocarbons, producing oxidants; hence II is true. It can irritate the eyes and respiratory tract, so III is false. Thus, I and II only.
